methodology.pub_fn_pattern: Directory-level ripgrep of literal `pub fn ` / `pub struct ` / `pub enum ` / `pub trait ` (literal substring — reliable across all files including nested subdirs `expr/` and `stmt/`)
methodology.dyn_unsafe_classification: Every `\bdyn\b` and `\bunsafe\b` content hit manually inspected to distinguish (a) real code, (b) string literals like `"unsafe"` keyword-token text in token.rs, (c) doc-comment keyword mentions in parser stmt_decl.rs, (d) Display-impl emitted keyword prefixes in ast/decl.rs. Only category (a) counts toward the verdict.

verdict_rules.GREEN: 0 real dyn-trait, 0 real unsafe, no FFI extern, AND pure data/logic (no fs I/O, no global state mutation, no subprocess spawn, no env-var reads in implementation)
verdict_rules.YELLOW: dyn-trait present but refactorable (e.g. callback → closure), OR clean pub API but implementation depends on OS-level facilities (fs / panic-hook / backtrace / subprocess / env) that Buff must provide via runtime intrinsics
verdict_rules.RED: dyn-trait in unavoidable public API position, OR real unsafe block, OR extern FFI declaration

purity_tiers.T1_pure_value: Returns Bool/Int/String/struct/ref/Option — no I/O, no global state, no process spawn, no env/TTY read
purity_tiers.T3_volatile: Reads process env, TTY state, system clock, or captures backtrace (non-deterministic; NONE of the 10 crates have time/UUID/random fields)
purity_tiers.T4_stateful: Mutates global state (panic hook), performs file I/O, spawns subprocess, or accumulates internal session state across calls

methodology.loc_source: Actual `Get-Content | Measure-Object -Line` over src/**/*.rs (task-spec LOC estimates were ~2x understated for parser: spec said 3640, actual is 7236)

purity_totals.note: ffi-guide has 0 pub fns (doc-only); 182+32+3+6 = 223 = total pub_fns

crates.name: buff-lang-ast

unsafe_usage.detail: Display impl writes literal `"unsafe "` prefix when formatting extern decls; doc strings describe Buff `unsafe` keyword semantics. NOT a Rust unsafe block.

crates.notes: Pure-data AST + IR graph (ir.rs: IrGraph/IrNode/AstLowerer with topological_order) + lossless trivia tree (lossless.rs: T57 byte-exact roundtrip). All 54 pub fns are constructors (new/empty/plain/named), accessors (span/len/is_empty/text/id), graph ops (add_node/add_dependency/dependencies/dependents/topological_order), or lossless-tree traversals (pieces/trivia/tokens/comments/piece_at/reparse). 14 T2 = Vec-returning (bindings, dependencies, dependents, topological_order, iterators). Zero I/O, zero global state. Direct port to Buff structs/enums + methods.

crates.name: buff-lang-ast-rsx
crates.notes: Pure-data RSX AST sibling crate (RsxTemplateFile + RsxNode 12-variant enum + RsxAttributeKind 7-variant + 14 struct kinds). 9 constructors (new/named/with_props returning Self) + 1 predicate (is_component_tag -> Bool). Trivial port — same shape as buff-lang-ast.

crates.name: buff-lang-error

volatile_fields.should_use_color: reads NO_COLOR env var (line 70) + std::io::IsTerminal (line 73) — process env + TTY state

crates.notes: LEAF crate (depended on by ALL other compiler crates). ErrorCode enum (E10xx/E11xx/E12xx/E13xx/E14xx/E15xx) is STABLE FOREVER — port the registry verbatim. 1 T3 fn: `should_use_color()` probes env+TTY; the API already offers `render_with_color(source, use_color: bool)` so Buff callers can bypass the env probe (pass use_color explicitly). 4 T2 fns: suggest_identifier -> Vec<String>, render_diagnostics -> String (technically T1 but included for batch), ErrorCode::all -> &'static [ErrorCode] (static slice). SourceMap + Span + Diagnostic + Levenshtein suggester (suggest.rs) are all pure compute. render_diagnostics_json emits deterministic JSON (BTreeMap-ordered).

volatile_fields.resolve_buff_map_path: reads BUFF_MAP_PATH env var + std::env::current_exe() — volatile env + exe path
volatile_fields.remap_panic_backtrace: uses std::backtrace::Backtrace — captures volatile runtime stack state

yellow_detail: format.rs::write_to_file / read_from_file use std::fs::write / std::fs::read_to_string (file I/O behind Result<_, std::io::Error>)

dyn_usage.detail: Type-name string used for formatting panic payloads; NOT an actual trait object in any signature

crates.notes: YELLOW: pub API has no dyn/unsafe/FFI in signatures, but IMPLEMENTATION depends on OS-level facilities Buff must provide via runtime intrinsics: (a) fs read/write of `.buffmap` sidecar, (b) global panic-hook installation, (c) runtime Backtrace capture. The 11 T1/T2 fns (SourceMap builders + lookups + JSON serialize/deserialize + build_source_map which walks the AST + formatted Rust source to build the mapping) port cleanly. Buff-side: panic hook may need a different mechanism since Buff runtime owns panic handling.

crates.name: buff-lang-lexer

yellow_detail.pub_fn: scan_string(source, quote_start, source_id, out, interp_cb: &mut dyn LexCallback) -> Result<usize, LexerError>
yellow_detail.refactor: Replace `&mut dyn LexCallback` with a Buff closure `Func` or fn pointer. Single-method trait (lex_range) — trivially desugars to a closure. NOT a blocker.

yellow_detail.detail: Required impl for Rust's std::error::Error trait — idiomatic, vanishes when ported to Buff's own Error trait model

dyn_usage.detail: Option<&(dyn std::error::Error + 'static)> — Rust's std::error::Error::source impl; universal pattern
DRIVES YELLOW VERDICT — `interp_cb: &mut dyn LexCallback` on pub fn scan_string. Single-method callback trait; refactorable to closure.

unsafe_usage.detail: Buff keyword token text — NOT a Rust unsafe block
Display impl formatting — NOT a Rust unsafe block

crates.notes: Hand-rolled byte-scanner (lexer.rs:39 tokenize -> Vec<Token>) + offside-rule indent tracker (indent.rs) + string-interpolation scanner (string_interp.rs: scan_string with LexCallback). YELLOW driver: pub fn scan_string takes `&mut dyn LexCallback` — refactor to closure. tokenize (T2 — Vec<Token>) is the main entry point and is pure. 12 T1 = LexerError constructors (new/unexpected_char/unterminated_string/invalid_number/mixed_tabs_spaces) + Token::new + TokenKind::from_keyword/is_keyword/all_keywords + indent ops. Port effort: low — replace 1 dyn callback.

crates.name: buff-lang-parser

unsafe_usage.detail: Documentation describing how the parser handles the Buff `unsafe` keyword token — NOT real unsafe code

crates.notes: Hand-rolled recursive-descent + Pratt parser. LARGEST target crate by both LOC (7236) and pub fn count (64). File layout: stream.rs (30 TokenStream cursor methods — peek/advance/expect/check/save/restore/sync_to_recovery_point), stmt/stmt_decl.rs (16 decl parsers — parse_func_decl/parse_struct_decl/parse_enum_decl/parse_trait_decl/parse_impl_decl/parse_extern_func_decl_with_abi/parse_attributes/...), parser.rs (5 top-level entries — parse/parse_with_edition/parse_recovering/parse_expression/parse_expression_with_edition), stmt.rs (4 — parse_statement/parse_block/parse_block_braces/parse_if_expr), expr/expr_postfix.rs (3 — parse_postfix/parse_call_args/parse_one_call_arg), expr/expr_pattern.rs (3 — parse_match/parse_pattern/parse_closure), options.rs (2 — Edition::is_scientific/require_for), expr.rs (1 — parse_expression). 9 T2 fns return Vec<Decl>/Vec<Param>/Vec<TypeParam>/Vec<Expr>/Vec<Attribute>. 55 T1 return single AST nodes or bool. NOTE: actual LOC=7236 (task spec said 3640 — spec was ~2x understated; parser grew through v1.x).

crates.name: buff-lang-buffhtml-parser
crates.notes: Hand-rolled 3-mode lexer (TEXT/TAG/BRACE) + recursive-descent parser for .buffhtml SFCs. Parallel pipeline to buff-lang-parser. Tiny public surface: parse -> RsxTemplateFile (T1), tokenize -> Vec<BuffHtmlToken> (T2), Token::new + Token::kind (T1), 3 BuffHtmlParseError helpers (lex/parse/span — T1). 1528-line lexer + 1228-line parser are mostly internal — only 7 fns escape to pub. Direct port — same algorithms as the GREEN main parser.

crates.name: buff-eval

volatile_fields.Evaluator.top_level_src: mutable String accumulating func/let declarations across calls
volatile_fields.Evaluator.body_stmts_src: mutable String accumulating body statements across calls

yellow_detail: Evaluator::eval / eval_line shell out to `rustc` via std::process::Command + spawn the compiled binary (subprocess I/O — requires Buff runtime primitive for process spawn + temp-file management)
Evaluator struct holds mutable session state (top_level_src + body_stmts_src) accumulated across eval/eval_line calls
Implementation reads BUFF_EVAL_BACKEND / BUFF_EVAL_TARGET / BUFF_EVAL_SCCACHE env vars; uses std::env::temp_dir + std::process::id for temp paths
Duplicates buff-lang-cli::pipeline::compile_rust_to_exe inline (avoiding clap/tokio transitive deps) — two copies must be kept in sync manually
crates.notes: YELLOW: pub API is clean (5 fns, 2 structs, no dyn/unsafe/FFI) but IMPLEMENTATION depends on (a) rustc subprocess spawn, (b) compiled-binary spawn + stdout capture, (c) temp-file write/cleanup, (d) mutable session state, (e) env-var-driven backend/target/sccache selection, (f) static AtomicU64 counter for unique temp stems. type_of() is pure (lex+parse+infer, no state mutation per docstring contract) and ports cleanly. eval/eval_line require a Buff runtime that can spawn rustc — non-trivial. Not RED because no hard-rule violations (no dyn/unsafe/extern in pub API). Semantic question for Buff port: the entire crate orchestrates rustc, which is the OPPOSITE of what Buff-native code does — in a self-hosted Buff, the eval engine would orchestrate the Buff compiler itself, likely a redesign rather than a literal port.

crates.name: buff-template
crates.notes: GREEN: tiny (150 LOC, 3 pub fns) wrapper over the pure-Rust `handlebars` crate. Designed FFI-guide compliant (R1–R6 — see compliance table in src/lib.rs module doc). Pub API is fully Buff-portable: from_string (T1 — pure compile), render (T1 — pure computation given compiled template), from_path (T4 — std::fs::read_to_string). catch_unwind is a Rust implementation detail of the FFI boundary, not a portability concern. Buff port: either (a) wrap the same handlebars Rust crate via Buff extern, or (b) reimplement a minimal template engine natively. The 3-fn surface is trivially portable either way.
